headline: High: Copilot can write repo files while Rasa may act on conversational outputs, creating default-pathway risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers and can write filesystem changes; Rasa ingests text/voice from external channels. A shared workspace or copied content could let attacker-controlled text influence Copilot-generated edits or downstream bot behavior. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Copilot Workspace edits are copied into Rasa training or response templates
IF Rasa ingests repository text or pasted prompts from the same operator workflow
mitigations: Separate bot content from code-review buffers
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into either agent
Require human review of any Copilot-generated file edits
Use a dedicated workspace for Rasa artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, while Rasa handles text and voice and can call external messaging APIs. If the same workspace or transcript content is reused across both, sensitive code or support text could flow into outputs or third-party channels. No direct shared-storage mechanism is documented, so this is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF the same files or transcripts are shared between Copilot and Rasa
IF Rasa forwards copied Copilot output into Slack, Telegram, or Twilio
mitigations: Keep code and support transcripts in separate folders
Redact secrets before moving text between agents
Restrict Rasa channels to non-sensitive test data
Review outbound messages before send
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Rasa has no documented write capability beyond allowlisted network egress and no multiple-instance support. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable-resource writes, so direct conflict is limited. Uncertainty about hidden orchestration or shared repos prevents a none verdict, but the documented overlap is small.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git working tree
IF Rasa is extended with file-writing tools outside the profile
mitigations: Run them in separate directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same branch
Use one writer at a time for repo changes
Lock the workspace during Copilot edits
requires-engineering: add file-locking or merge coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot Workspace proposes edits for human review, and Rasa’s dialogue pipeline can treat upstream text as authoritative if integrated naively. If Copilot output is fed into Rasa responses or actions without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect customer-facing replies. The review step lowers severity below high, but the pathway exists in default-style integrations.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated text is used as Rasa response content
IF Rasa sends messages without a verification step
mitigations: Require explicit approval before Rasa sends any generated reply
Compare Copilot output against source files before reuse
Log provenance for imported text
Limit Copilot output to draft-only artifacts
requires-engineering: add validation rules before outbound actions

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is documented as vendor-hosted with GitHub repo context, while Rasa is open-source and can be deployed on allowlisted channels. The profiles do not show a concrete residency or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance risk is supportable. The other agent is cited because the concern is about cross-agent data handling, but no specific violation is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents without a deployment policy
IF Rasa is hosted in a jurisdiction that conflicts with the data source
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent
Keep regulated data out of Copilot and Rasa test flows
Document retention settings for both systems
Review vendor and hosting locations
requires-engineering: formalize residency and DPA checks
